It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

last_dated_appearance.note: NO SIGHTING, SO THE LEG IS A SOURCE'S SPAN. The card holds no dated reading of this person at or before the scene date; the date here is the far end of what a cited source COVERS, which the role's own note calls the source's bound and not the man's. Read from `roles[] (source_span)` as `1833-11/1835-08`, which reaches 1835-08-31 — a window that covers 1835-07-01 itself, so it pins no last sighting before the day and cannot be read as one. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Last printed 1835-05-20, at the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13, and nothing reached either follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. A documented resident whose whereabouts on one day are unknown is `uncertain` here rather than dropped: that is the same distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and it is a finding rather than a gap.

occupation.note: THE TRADE IS THE PAPER'S. The corpus reads it as sheriff of Cook county, sheriff, at the Democrat of 3 September 1834, column 6; the Democrat of 18 March 1834, column 2; the Democrat of 1 April 1834, column 22; the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13. The residents vocabulary's nearest period-correct word for it is `sheriff`, and where the corpus prints more than one trade they are all named here rather than reduced to the one the vocabulary could take.

dated_bounds.identity_rule: data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json — persons[] person_forbes_stephen, action `enrich` onto this card. The register states its own reason there and this row cites it rather than transcribing it.
dated_bounds.note: AN APPEARANCE IN THE TOWN'S PRINT, AND NOTHING FURTHER. The Chicago Democrat of 1834-09-03 names 'Stephen Forbes' in the claim read as chicago_democrat_1834_09_03#c006, so the reading dates an appearance of this person in the town's press and `here_by` is null: a name in print is not a body in the town, and a notice can be signed elsewhere and reprinted here. Under the evidence ladder ratified 2026-09-03 a source EARLIER than the scene date corroborates and dates and never promotes, and a source LATER than it does not promote either. THE IDENTITY IS INFERRED AND THE PAGE IS NOT: the issue is deposited, dated and numbered in data/research/newspapers/corpus.json, and what no source states is that the name the paper prints is the person on this card — the register joins them under its own written note. No grade moves here and the identity is neither reopened nor hardened.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'Stephen Forbes' and 'Stephen Forbes, Sheriff' and 'Vorbes, Stephan' and 'its, directed to Stephen Forbes; Sheeift' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 3 September 1834, column 6; the Democrat of 18 March 1834, column 2; the Democrat of 1 April 1834, column 22; the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13. The corpus associates the name with Cook County; that is where the paper does business with this person and not a statement about where they slept, and the storefront tickets are the ones that may stand a shop there. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `sheriff` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the city register of 1839 — “Stephen Forbes” as sheriff of cook county, 1832 (f1839_r0088, printed page 39). What a match may carry, and it depends on WHICH TABLE it landed in. A match on printed page 38, or on any row of the mayors' table, is 1839-or-later evidence: it says the man held that office in that year and was therefore in Chicago in that year, it is written with the row's own describes_date and never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on it alone — a later appearance is corroboration of CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not of July 1835. A match on the sheriffs' rows of 1831, 1832, 1834 or 1836 is different in kind: the office is contemporary with the town, the 1834 row's term covers the scene date outright, and such a match carries reaches_scene. Even there the SOURCE is a retrospect — a table running to 1874, set in 1876 out of Old Settlers' recollections per the compiler's warning on printed page 3 — so it may be cited as a contemporary office and may not be graded `documented` without a second, nearer record. The ward on printed page 38 is a ward of the CITY of 1839 and places no house in the town of 1835. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Forbes' folds to the same string as the register entry's, and the given name of both begins S. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

roles.note: AN OFFICE FROM THE FERGUS 1839 CITY REGISTER, carried here by its own crosswalk (T-1254, by tools/derive_resident_roles.py). The register is a retrospective table set in 1876, and its carry rule is explicit: a later office is corroboration of CONTINUED RESIDENCE and never an 1835 fact. The crosswalk marks this row as reaching the scene date and the volume is one this card already stands on.

THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

age_band.note: THE BAND THIS PERSON'S OWN BIRTH YEAR PUTS THEM IN on 1 July 1835. It is a view of a value already on this card and adds nothing to it; it exists so the age axis can be read across the whole layer at once, beside the bands the model draws for everybody else.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'Stephen' is read as male because 1 person in this layer whose sex a source records bears it (gale_stephen_f). Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.

birth_year.note: A BIRTH INTERVAL OUT OF A DEATH NOTICE, NOT A RECORD OF A BIRTH. The page prints the death as 'February 11, 1879' and the age as 'aged 81¾'. An age of 81 years and 9 months means at least that and less than 81 years and 10 months, so the birth falls between 1797-04-12 and 1797-05-11: the birth year is 1797. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints the entry "Forbes, Stephen VanRensselaer, died February 11, 1879, aged 81¾.", and its header admits the list also names citizens who arrived after 1843 and others merely prominently connected with Illinois history — so a match here is never evidence of residence in 1835 and never moves a grade. The match to this person was adjudicated in data/research/old_settlers/death_notices_crosswalk_1835.json and written onto this card by tools/spend_old_settlers.py; this pass only spends its arithmetic into a birth year. Both sides of the match spell a forename out — the crosswalk's thin matches, where a single initial is the whole of the discriminator, are refused rather than spent.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0376), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name Stephen Forbes as a sheriff at Chicago 4 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. Reading a family, a house or a quarter of town into this record would be reading something the papers do not say. tools/mint_documented_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.

Names, places * , dates, and ages at death
of some of Chicago's Old Settlers, prior to 1843, and other well - known citizens who arrived after 1843, together

old_settler_deaths.note: LATER EVIDENCE OF A DEATH, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints an obituary list of old settlers, and one of its entries meets somebody of this name. THE HEADER OF THE LIST IS QUOTED ABOVE, and it is the limit the whole reading turns on. It does not mean the person was in Chicago in 1835, and it does not mean they arrived before 1843 — the list's own header, quoted above, says it also names citizens who arrived later and others merely 'prominently connected with Illinois history'. A match means one thing: a name in the 1835 layer and a name in this list agree on surname and first initial, and the list gives that name a death date and an age. The date and the interval are the payload. Whatever is carried is carried as evidence of a DEATH and of an interval the birth falls in, never as an 1835 fact and never as a grade. T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply; this file changes no record. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. A death notice printed in 1896 says a person of this name died on a day; under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that is later evidence about a DEATH, and it is never an 1835 residence. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.
